defillama_probe.publication_lag_verdict: INSUFFICIENT EVIDENCE from a single response for every endpoint probed. See reprobe_experiment for what two spaced responses did show.

caveats.observed: api.binance.com returned HTTP 451 ('Service unavailable from a restricted location') to every request from this container, including /api/v3/ping, /api/v3/klines and /api/v3/exchangeInfo. 3 attempts per symbol for exchangeInfo, all 451.
caveats.impact: No kline was taken from the live REST API. All Binance OHLCV here comes from the data.binance.vision archive instead. Anything that must come from the live API (order-book, instrument filters, server time) is absent.
caveats.what_a_backtest_could_get_wrong: Assuming these CSVs and a live /api/v3/klines pull are interchangeable. They are the same underlying bars, but the archive lags (see archive-publication-lag) and carries no instrument metadata.

caveats.observed: tickSize, stepSize, minNotional, status and permitted order types were NOT obtained for either symbol. The two exchangeinfo_*.UNAVAILABLE.json files are attempt records, not instrument data.
caveats.impact: Price/qty rounding, minimum order size and order-type support are UNKNOWN in this dataset.
caveats.what_a_backtest_could_get_wrong: Simulating fills at prices or sizes the venue would reject, or assuming a default tick/step. There is no evidence here for any tick or step value - do not guess one.

caveats.observed: The archive contains no bars for the current UTC day. Latest 1h bar is 2026-11-08T23:00:00Z (closing 2026-11-08T23:59:59Z); the daily archive object for 2026-11-09 returned HTTP 404 while the 2026-11-08 object was present. Snapshot taken at 2026-11-09T17:22:00Z.
caveats.impact: Data ends roughly 18 hours before wall clock, and the lag varies with when the archive publishes.
caveats.what_a_backtest_could_get_wrong: Treating the last row as 'now'. A live system reading these files would act on stale state. No still-forming bar needed dropping here precisely because the archive never contained one.

caveats.observed: Binance archive open_time/close_time switched from milliseconds to MICROSECONDS exactly at 2025-01-01T00:00:00Z. Last millisecond bar: 2024-12-31T23:00:00Z. Both units appear within one series: {'us': 16992, 'ms': 64525} rows (counts include the monthly/daily overlap).
caveats.impact: Handled here by magnitude detection (>1e14 => microseconds). The shipped CSVs are uniformly ISO-8601 UTC.
caveats.what_a_backtest_could_get_wrong: Re-parsing the raw archives with a fixed unit=ms assumption. 1735689600000000 read as milliseconds is the year 56960; read as seconds it is the year 1970. Any new archive ingest must detect the unit per row, not per file.

caveats.observed: 43 consecutive 1h bars, 2018-02-09T09:28:14Z through 2018-02-11T03:28:14Z, are offset from the hour grid by 1694789 ms (28 m 14.789 s). They are hourly-spaced but not hour-aligned, and realign at 2018-02-11T04:00:00Z. Identical in BTCUSDT and ETHUSDT. Follows the 32-bar outage gap ending 2018-02-09.
caveats.impact: timestamp % 3600 != 0 for those 43 rows.
caveats.what_a_backtest_could_get_wrong: Resampling or joining on hour boundaries will silently drop or misalign these bars; a reindex to a regular hourly grid will insert 43 NaN rows and discard real data. Any 'bars are on the grid' assertion fails here.

caveats.observed: In each 1h series, 15 bars have closeTime - openTime != 1 h, measured on the raw archive. Durations run from 14.8 s (2018-01-04T03:00:00Z, BTCUSDT) up to 2,454,774 ms (2021-02-11T03:00:00Z), and one bar has a NEGATIVE duration: 2020-12-21T14:00:00Z closes at 2020-12-21T13:47:20.521Z, 12 m 39 s BEFORE it opens. Full list per symbol in files[...].integrity.bar_duration_anomalies. The anomalies sit at outage boundaries and are near-identical between BTCUSDT and ETHUSDT (they differ only in milliseconds).
caveats.impact: A bar labelled 1h can represent 15 seconds of trading, or an inconsistent interval, or carry a corrupt closeTime. The shipped CSVs keep openTime only, so the defect is invisible in them.
caveats.what_a_backtest_could_get_wrong: Treating every row as one hour of exposure, and treating per-bar volume or range as comparable across rows. A 14.8-second bar's volume and high-low range are not an hourly observation; using them in a volatility or liquidity estimate injects outliers that are artefacts. It also means Binance's own closeTime field is not trustworthy in this dataset - the drop-the-forming-bar rule leans on exactly that field.

caveats.observed: 43 bars (the same Feb-2018 window) have sub-second open times, e.g. 2018-02-09T09:28:14.789Z. The required output format is second precision, so .789 is truncated.
caveats.impact: Those timestamps in the CSV are up to 789 ms earlier than the venue's actual bar open.
caveats.what_a_backtest_could_get_wrong: Round-tripping the CSV back to milliseconds and expecting it to match the archive byte-for-byte. It will not, for those 43 rows.

caveats.observed: The 1h series has 29 gaps totalling 126 missing bars, all between 2017-09-06 and 2023-03-24, identical in both symbols. Largest is 32 bars ending 2018-02-09. The 1d series has 0 gaps.
caveats.impact: The hourly series is NOT contiguous. Full gap list is in this manifest under files['binance/BTCUSDT_1h.csv'].integrity.gaps.
caveats.what_a_backtest_could_get_wrong: Computing rolling windows or returns by row position rather than by timestamp. A 24-row window spanning a gap covers more than 24 hours of real time. Bars are absent, not zero-volume.

caveats.observed: October 2026 is published both as a monthly archive and as 31 per-day archives, producing 31 duplicate timestamps in the 1d source and 744 in the 1h source. Value conflicts between the two: 0 and 0.
caveats.impact: Deduplicated on timestamp; duplicate_timestamps is 0 in every shipped CSV. The zero conflict count means the monthly and daily archives agree exactly on every overlapping bar.
caveats.what_a_backtest_could_get_wrong: Concatenating monthly and daily archives without dedup, which double-counts a month of bars.

caveats.observed: The volume column is archive field 5 = base asset volume (BTC or ETH). Quote-asset volume (field 7), trade count (field 8) and taker-buy splits (fields 9-10) exist in the source and were NOT carried into these CSVs. Kraken's volume is its OHLC field index 6, also base volume; its field index 5 (vwap) was discarded.
caveats.impact: volume is in coins, not dollars, on both venues.
caveats.what_a_backtest_could_get_wrong: Reading volume as notional/USD, which inflates it by roughly the price. Cross-venue volume is comparable in units but not in meaning: Binance BTCUSDT volume and Kraken XBTUSD volume are different books.

caveats.observed: Binance pairs quote in USDT; Kraken pairs quote in USD. The requested basis metric therefore measures venue dislocation AND USDT/USD deviation together. Measured over the same 720 days, |USDT/USD - 1| had a median of 3.3 bps and a max of 23.5 bps. Re-running the comparison with the Binance close converted at Kraken's USDT/USD daily close drops the BTC median from 4.2694 to 1.2944 bps and the p95 from 14.6778 to 6.061 bps.
caveats.impact: Roughly three quarters of the headline basis is the stablecoin leg, not the venues disagreeing on the price of BTC.
caveats.what_a_backtest_could_get_wrong: Sizing a cross-venue arbitrage or a slippage allowance off the headline number, and in doing so taking USDT redemption risk it never priced. Also: treating USDT and USD as the same unit of account when netting PnL across venues.

caveats.observed: api.kraken.com /0/public/OHLC returned only 721 daily bars per pair - the endpoint's ~720-bar trailing window. After dropping the forming final bar, the shipped files span 2024-11-19T00:00:00Z to 2026-11-08T00:00:00Z. This is the documented endpoint limit and was not worked around.
caveats.impact: The cross-venue check covers 720 days, against 3371 days of Binance history. 2651 Binance days have no Kraken counterpart.
caveats.what_a_backtest_could_get_wrong: Generalising the measured basis to the pre-2024 era. It is unmeasured there, and the 2024-2026 window contains no event comparable to, say, the March 2020 or May 2021 dislocations.

caveats.observed: Kraken returned a bar for 2026-11-09T00:00:00Z whose day had not closed; it was dropped from all three Kraken CSVs. Kraken's result also carries a 'last' field (XBTUSD: 1794096000 = 2026-11-08T00:00:00Z), which is a continuation cursor, not a data boundary.
caveats.impact: Shipped Kraken files end on the last fully closed UTC day.
caveats.what_a_backtest_could_get_wrong: Keeping Kraken's final bar, which is a partial day and whose close is simply the price at fetch time. Mixing it with Binance's completed bars creates a look-ahead-free but simply wrong last row.

caveats.observed: Price and volume values are copied verbatim from each venue. Binance uses fixed 8-decimal strings ('4261.48000000'); Kraken uses variable precision ('90508.0', '92538.5').
caveats.impact: No float round-trip was introduced, but the two venues' files are not byte-comparable and string sorting of values is meaningless.
caveats.what_a_backtest_could_get_wrong: String equality or hash comparison of prices across venues; assuming a fixed decimal width when parsing.

caveats.observed: One of 636 archive requests (BTCUSDT 1d 2021-04) failed with a connection error rather than a 404 on the first pass, and succeeded on retry. Without the present/404 distinction it would have been indistinguishable from 'month does not exist'.
caveats.impact: All 600 archive objects used here were fetched and every one was verified against its published .zip.CHECKSUM sha256 (0 mismatches).
caveats.what_a_backtest_could_get_wrong: An ingest loop that treats any non-200 as 'no data for that month' will produce a silently short series that still looks well-formed. Row counts must be asserted, not assumed.

caveats.observed: None of the five endpoints returns an as-of, published-at, revision or finality field. The only time-related HTTP headers are Date and Age; Age is CDN cache age (observed 236-263 s), which says nothing about the staleness or finality of the underlying data. Every daily series' last point is dated 2026-11-09T00:00:00Z, i.e. the current UTC day, 17.4 h before the probe.
caveats.impact: INSUFFICIENT EVIDENCE: publication lag cannot be determined from a response alone.
caveats.what_a_backtest_could_get_wrong: Point-in-time correctness. If the last daily point is a running intraday figure that is later revised, any strategy reading the series as-of that date is using a number that did not exist, in that form, on that date. Nothing in the response distinguishes a final value from a provisional one.

caveats.observed: historicalChainTvl returns 138 leading days with tvl exactly 0, from 2017-09-27 to 2018-02-11; first non-zero is 2018-02-12T00:00:00Z. Identical count for the all-chain and Ethereum series. Those are the only zero values in either series.
caveats.impact: The series' nominal start is 138 days earlier than its informative start.
caveats.what_a_backtest_could_get_wrong: Computing percentage change or a log ratio off a zero base (division by zero or infinite return), or reading those zeros as 'measured no TVL' rather than 'no coverage'.

caveats.observed: stablecoincharts/all: 'date' is a JSON STRING of unix seconds, whereas historicalChainTvl's 'date' is an int. The peg-key set inside totalCirculating grows from 1 key in the first record to 30 in the last (30 distinct keys across the series). Three distinct top-level key sets occur: 476 records lack totalUnreleased, and totalMintedUSD/totalBridgedToUSD appear in exactly ONE record - the final one.
caveats.impact: The record schema is not stable along the series.
caveats.what_a_backtest_could_get_wrong: Fixing columns from the first (or last) record. Inferring from the first record drops 29 pegs; inferring from the last expects two fields that exist nowhere else. Also: summing totalCirculating across peg keys adds EUR to JPY to USD - use totalCirculatingUSD for anything denominated.

caveats.observed: excludeTotalDataChart=true empties totalDataChart (length 0) but totalDataChartBreakdown is still returned in full (4649 daily points, 2014-02-17 to 2026-11-09), alongside 1587 protocol records of 35 fields each. Observed response: 21,259,901 bytes (20.3 MiB).
caveats.impact: The parameter does not make this endpoint cheap. Breakdown values mix int and float across entries (384 entries all-float, 3458 all-int, 807 mixed).
caveats.what_a_backtest_could_get_wrong: Polling this endpoint on a schedule, or in a loop per chain, and assuming it is light. Also: the breakdown's value shape is {protocol_name: usd_volume}, not chain-nested, despite the field name.

caveats.observed: totalDataChartBreakdown's earliest point is 2014-02-17 with value {'Counterparty DEX': 6.23}, years before the AMM era.
caveats.impact: Early history is a single obscure venue at single-digit dollar volumes.
caveats.what_a_backtest_could_get_wrong: Normalising or computing growth rates from the series start, which is dominated by near-zero values from one protocol rather than a market-wide measure.

caveats.observed: coins.llama.fi/prices/current returns a single point: price (USD), symbol, timestamp (unix seconds - an observation time, not a bar boundary) and confidence (0-1, meaning not defined by the response). Observed size 112 bytes.
caveats.impact: No history and no bar semantics.
caveats.what_a_backtest_could_get_wrong: Using it as a close. It is whatever the oracle last saw, at an arbitrary second within the day, and 'confidence' is unexplained - its scale and failure mode are undocumented in the response.

caveats.observed: Bar-dropping and lag figures are computed against the container clock, which agreed with DefiLlama's returned price timestamp to within about 3 minutes and with Kraken's and the CDN's Date headers.
caveats.impact: Lag numbers carry a few minutes of clock uncertainty.
caveats.what_a_backtest_could_get_wrong: Treating 'drop the bar if closeTime is in the future' as exact when the local clock is wrong. On a skewed clock that rule can keep a forming bar or drop a complete one.

caveats.observed: The same newest daily point (dated 2026-11-09T00:00:00Z) was read three times from /v2/historicalChainTvl and its VALUE changed. All-chain tvl: 79,003,625,907 served 17:24:25Z (CDN cache age 243 s), then 79,021,985,782 served 17:26:10Z (cache age 1 s) - a move of 18,359,875 USD (2.3239 bps) - then unchanged at 17:41:11Z. Ethereum tvl moved 19,385,019 USD (4.6206 bps) over the same interval. Point count stayed at 3331 and the point's date never changed. stablecoincharts/all's totalCirculatingUSD.peggedUSD did NOT move across the three reads (293,008,620,022.67). prices/current moved as expected for a spot quote.
caveats.impact: Measured, not inferred: the daily point dated for the current UTC day is PROVISIONAL and is revised while that day is still running. The response gives no way to tell a revised value from a settled one, and the revision does not bump any version, date or count field.
caveats.what_a_backtest_could_get_wrong: Point-in-time correctness. A backtest that reads the series today and treats the last row as the value that was knowable on that date is using a number that did not exist in that form at any point during the day. Re-running the same backtest hours later silently produces different results from the same code and the same date range. Either drop the newest point, or snapshot and store what was actually served at the time. Note the inverse too: the 15-minute interval with no change is NOT evidence of finality - it only bounds the update cadence from below.

raw.note: Three observations of the SAME newest daily data point, same field, at three times. Age is the CDN cache age of that response in seconds.
